Subject: Quick follow-up from today's demo

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Craig and I appreciated the walkthrough of Redwood's latency guarantees and the cost controls. We have a couple of follow-up questions as we scope the pilot: 

- Primary constraint: patient PHI will be involved; we need to understand options that meet our security/legal team requirements (SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration, VPC/private deployment).
- Expected latency: our UI requires 100–200ms p99 for short queries (~50 tokens). How well will Hosted API meet that?
- Timeline: leadership wants a 6-week pilot if we can scope it this quarter.

Can you send a concise recommendation for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for our use case, and a draft PoC plan (success criteria + stakeholders + minimal data access reqs)? Also flag any blockers for an on-prem evaluation.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo

Elena —

Great to meet you and Craig yesterday. Below is a short recommendation and a proposed PoC scaffold — happy to iterate once you confirm internal stakeholders and any non-negotiable compliance constraints.

Recommendation (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to run but requires you to accept our hosted environment policy; acceptable if PHI can be tokenized or if you prefer no persistent storage.
- Dedicated: good middle ground — reserved GPU pools in our cloud with network-level isolation and stricter logging controls; often hits p99 targets for low-latency UIs with tuned batching.
- Private VPC / On-prem: recommended if your legal/compliance team requires customer-managed networking or air-gapped processing (more setup/time/cost).

Proposed PoC (6 weeks):
1) Week 0 — Kickoff & access: confirm PoC dataset, sign simple NDA + SOC 2 snapshot review, tech contacts for networking.
2) Week 1 — Baseline test: smoke run on Hosted API with synthetic PHI-masked dataset to measure p50/p95/p99.
3) Week 2–3 — Dedicated run (if you want reserved capacity): run production-like batch and latency tests; enable KV cache and observe throughput.
4) Week 4 — Private VPC dry-run (optional): short validation of network tunnels and KMS integration for keys.
5) Week 5–6 — QA, stakeholder demo, success criteria validation, pass/fail decision.

Success criteria (draft):
- Latency: p99 <= 250ms for 50-token queries on Dedicated; Hosted p99 <= 350ms acceptable for early tests.
- Accuracy: model responses meet your labeling set F1 >= 0.85 on target prompts.
- Security: SOC 2 evidence reviewed + KMS support for keys in Private or Dedicated config.
- Ops: ability to replay / audit requests for 30 days.

Primary asks from Atlas:
- Confirm who will own security sign-off and legal (name + email).
- Dataset access: will you provide a redacted sample or do we need to set up a S3 read-only integration?
- Target PoC start week (we can aim for the week of Nov 9).

I'll attach a short runbook and our SOC 2 snapshot. Marissa and Aditya — looping you in to validate resource commitments and cost estimate (very rough) for Dedicated.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — Elena
